title: CARL: Criticality-Aware Agentic Reinforcement Learning
trick: Rank states by how uncertain the policy is about its next action, start new rollouts only from the most uncertain ones so rollouts form a tree, credit each action by child-minus-parent average outcome, and drop sibling-less actions from the update.
framing_stripped: Called criticality-aware RL; criticality is defined as the fork-measured outcome spread and then replaced by action entropy as a proxy.
load_bearing_assumption: Action entropy correlates with how much the ending depends on the action (validated only at the distribution level, Cliff's delta 0.42; confident-wrong decisions are invisible by their own limitations section).
weakest_component: The proxy substitution: the definition is the right quantity; the measurement is entropy. No validation at the state level against the defined quantity.
regime: Multi-turn search agents on knowledge QA (NQ, HotpotQA, TriviaQA, MuSiQue; GAIA OOD); Qwen2.5 3B/7B, Qwen3-4B; ~5 turns; +~2 F1 over GRPO with 82% more rollout actions and 56% of update samples.
information_asymmetry: The defined criticality (outcome spread across actions) exists only after continuations; the paper never asks whether any training-time information predicts it other than entropy.
occupies: Entropy-placed tree forking with selective update on search agents.

neighbors.trick: Group steps that landed in the same state across rollouts.
Branch by the between-actions variance per cost, estimated from pilots.

theme_fit.why: a baseline placement rule and a statement of our question

limitations_as_complaints: If the model is confidently wrong, entropy will not flag the state.
